NODE_FASTA_FILE.description: FASTA whose records become the layout's nodes. Only network nodes named in it are laid out (matched by full sanitized header or its first word); usually the FASTA the network was built from. Pass absolute paths: a relative one resolves under the project's Input_Files/Sequence_Sets when it exists there, else under the project root, never under the user's saved Config directories.

INPUT_HDF5.description: Network file from align_similarity_matrix, network_injection, network_extraction, align_substitution_matrix or parse_blast_output. Pass an absolute path: a relative one resolves under the project's Input_Files/Networks_EValues when it exists there, else under the project root.

ALIGNMENT_SCORE.description: Embedding-alignment networks only (ignored for E-value networks): global (Needleman-Wunsch, full-length similarity) or local (Smith-Waterman, best matching region; suits multi-domain proteins).

NORM_MODE.description: Embedding-alignment networks only: divisor applied to the raw alignment score. local scores cannot use alignment_length. longer_sequence penalizes length differences most; shorter_sequence lets a fragment score highly against a longer relative.

SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD.description: Physics layouts: keep edges whose score is at least this value. Units depend on the network: the normalized alignment score for embedding networks, -log10(E-value) for E-value networks. Ignored when TOP_EDGE_PERCENT is set or UMAP_MODE is true.

TOP_EDGE_PERCENT.description: Physics layouts: keep the best N percent of all possible pairs among the laid-out nodes (N(N-1)/2, not the stored pairs); the cutoff becomes the Nth-best score. Overrides SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD.

UMAP_MODE.description: true computes coordinates with UMAP from each node's strongest edges instead of the physics simulation; edge filters are then ignored.

UMAP_NEIGHBORS.description: UMAP only: other nodes per neighborhood. Smaller values emphasize local subclusters, larger values global structure.

UMAP_MIN_DIST.description: UMAP only: minimum spacing of points; lower packs clusters tighter.

LAYOUT_DIMENSIONS.description: 2 for the desktop Viewer; 3 only for the optional VR viewer (stored in a separate _3D cache folder).

LAYOUT_SEED.description: Random seed for reproducible coordinates; null gives an unseeded run.

LAYOUT_DEVICE_SELECTION.description: Compute device for the physics simulation. auto first runs a short benchmark (seconds for small networks) and may pick a different backend per component-size class.

DT.description: Integration time step. Smaller is more stable but needs more steps; unused when AUTO_DT is true.

AUTO_DT.description: true gives each simulation stage the largest stable time step computed from its springs and repulsion; DT is then ignored.

MAX_STEPS.description: Upper limit of simulation steps per stage; simulations usually stop earlier on convergence.

RMSD_THRESHOLD.description: Stop when the mean node displacement per step falls below this value.

PERCENTAGE_DROP_THRESHOLD.description: After a quarter of MAX_STEPS, stop when the averaged RMSD fell by less than this percentage over the last RMSD_WINDOW steps; 0 disables it.

RMSD_WINDOW.description: Steps over which the RMSD plateau test is averaged.

ENABLE_PROGRESSIVE_SIMULATION.description: Large components only (over 2,000 nodes): anneal by lowering the similarity threshold in stages, which helps dense components untangle into subclusters.

SPRING_K.description: Attraction of every kept edge (all edges pull equally; scores only decide which edges are kept).

COULOMB_K.description: Repulsion between nodes of the same component; larger values spread clusters out.

COULOMB_CUTOFF.description: Distance beyond which repulsion is ignored; lower is faster.

DAMPING.description: Velocity damping; higher values settle oscillations faster.

MAX_FORCE_LIMIT.description: Cap on each pairwise force (hidden in the Config GUI; keep the default).

MAX_TOTAL_REPULSION_FORCE.description: Cap on the summed repulsion per node; 0 disables the cap (hidden in the Config GUI; keep the default).

PACKING_GEOMETRY.description: Arrangement of separate components around the largest one.

PACKING_GRID_SIZE.description: Grid cell used to pack components; smaller packs tighter but slower.

BOX_SCALE.description: Initial simulation box scale (hidden in the Config GUI; raise it only if the log asks for more room).

PACKING_PADDING.description: Clearance kept between packed components (hidden in the Config GUI).

SAVED_LAYOUT_DIR.description: Root folder of layout caches; each input/filter combination gets its own subfolder with a cache_manifest.json. Default: the user's saved Config directory, else Cache_Files/Saved_Layouts.

TARGET_CACHE_PATH.description: Set by export and by the finished job; a layout job always publishes a new cache file.

CACHE_FILENAME.description: Cache file name; with CACHE_NAME_MODE auto the next free version_NN.h5 is chosen when the job runs.

CACHE_NAME_MODE.description: auto picks the next free version; explicit uses CACHE_FILENAME and fails if that file exists.

rules: A physics layout needs SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD or TOP_EDGE_PERCENT; TOP_EDGE_PERCENT wins when both are set, and UMAP ignores both.
Embedding-alignment networks need ALIGNMENT_SCORE and NORM_MODE; local scores cannot use alignment_length.
A layout job never overwrites a cache; caches with the same inputs and edge filter share a folder as version_00.h5, version_01.h5, ...
gui_range is the Config GUI's slider range; the job accepts any value meeting the minimum and maximum.
choosing_an_edge_filter: Call network_statistics with the network, the node FASTA and the intended ALIGNMENT_SCORE and NORM_MODE before choosing a threshold. It returns the score distribution and, for a range of cutoffs, the kept edges, clusters, isolated nodes and largest cluster.

A cutoff that leaves one cluster holding nearly every node shows little substructure, while one that isolates most nodes shows little relationship; intermediate cutoffs usually separate subfamilies. Prefer the user's scientific criterion when given; on an E-value network an E-value cutoff converts as SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD = -log10(E), so 1e-20 becomes 20.
TOP_EDGE_PERCENT adapts to any score scale and is a reasonable first choice when no statistics are available; report the effective threshold from the job result.
